## On your arithmetic question

The "last quarter" column in the report (three months ended 30 Sep 2026) prints the basic EPS as **١٩٩**. The OCR flag on that cell notes a decimal comma may have been dropped, so the intended figure is most likely **1.99 EGP** per share.

Multiplying 1.99 × 4 gives **7.96 EGP**.

However, I have to flag two things before you treat that as a "yearly earnings" number:

1. **The source figure is ambiguous.** The report's own OCR note says the decimal mark is uncertain. If the true print were 199 (no decimal), the ×4 result would be 796 EGP – a completely different order of magnitude.
2. **The method is unreliable.** A single quarter × 4 does not equal a full year. The same report already shows 9-month EPS of **8.74 EGP** (verified). If Q3 were truly 1.99, then Q1+Q2 would have to be 8.74 − 1.99 = 6.75 EGP, meaning Q3 is a *weak* quarter, not a representative one. Annualising it would *understate* the year. Conversely, if Q3 were a spike, ×4 would *overstate* it. The 9-month figure (8.74) plus an actual Q4 print is the only honest way to get a full-year number.

I'm not going to build a valuation or earnings forecast on top of that, as that's company-financials analysis outside my remit.

## Investor-suitability read (what the portfolio allows)

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Horizon vs. goal** | 3 years to hold ABUK for income is workable; you're not forced to sell on a short-term dip. |
| **Liquidity buffer** | You keep a separate emergency fund, so the 10,000 EGP cash and the ABUK position are *not* earmarked for emergencies. That's clean. |
| **Loss tolerance / capacity** | Both rated **medium**. A single-stock position at ~60 % of the portfolio (see below) sits at the upper edge of what "medium" comfortably absorbs. A 30 % drawdown on ABUK would cut total portfolio value by roughly 18 %. |
| **Current concentration** | ABUK: 200 × 76.21 = **15,242 EGP**. Cash: **10,000 EGP**. Total: **25,242 EGP**. ABUK is **≈ 60 %** of the portfolio – a single-name concentration that a medium-loss-tolerance profile would normally want to keep below ~50 %. |
| **What is free / sellable** | • 10,000 EGP cash is immediately deployable. • All 200 ABUK shares are unencumbered and could be sold (≈ 15,242 EGP) if you chose to rebalance. |
| **Reasonable cash commitment** | Given the medium loss capacity and the existing 60 % single-stock tilt, committing the full 10,000 EGP into *another* equity (or more ABUK) would push concentration further. A more conservative read is that only a portion of the 10,000 EGP – perhaps 3,000–5,000 EGP – could be committed to a new position without breaching the medium-loss comfort zone, leaving the rest as a buffer. |

### Bottom line for suitability
The 3-year income-hold on ABUK is directionally fine, and your separate emergency fund removes the liquidity pressure. The main suitability tension is **concentration**: at ~60 % in one name with medium loss tolerance, the portfolio has limited room to absorb a further equity allocation before the risk profile drifts beyond what "medium" implies. The 10,000 EGP cash is free, but deploying it all into additional equity would deepen the single-stock exposure rather than diversify it.

*I'm not recommending a buy, sell, or hold – that's the team's call. This is just the suitability frame.*
